description: SASRec predicts the next interaction using item and positional embeddings, causal self-attention, and feed-forward layers. Attention selects relevant past interactions, adapting between recent context and longer histories. Candidate scores use dot products with learned item embeddings. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: Sparse histories favor simple transition patterns, while richer histories can support longer dependencies. SASRec learns which history positions matter. Despite the supplied title, this is a sequential recommendation baseline, not a dedicated solution for users or items without interactions.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain separate models and routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the environment's 200-epoch default. Select changes using only the pinned macro validation HR@10 within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer whenever architecture changes. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); diagnostics must use measured values and available inputs. No benchmark improvement has been established.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark splits.
  Initialize the category's SASRec model using training seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Embed the padded history and its positions.
    Apply causal attention and feed-forward blocks.
    Score shifted positive items and sampled negatives.
    Optimize sampled binary cross-entropy over valid positions.
  Save model weights and architecture configuration beneath the trial directory.
Generate working/predict.py with matching architecture and category routing.
Use the host's macro validation HR@10 to compare trials.

originality.positive: The paper introduces an effective application of self-attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: The supplied task starts from SASRec and specifies no new cold-start mechanism; reproducing it adds little methodological novelty. Scores use a qualitative 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: The baseline supports controlled experiments with regularization, sequence length, sampling, and permitted item content.
future_potential.negative: Improvements require measured validation evidence; learned item identifiers alone provide limited support for unseen items.

code_difficulty.positive: An existing per-dataset SASRec baseline reduces implementation effort.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes must remain consistent across training, diagnostic compatibility methods, checkpoint loading, and generated inference. Higher scores indicate greater difficulty.
